newsitem.title: UK: Urals trade at distressed level due to May avails.
newsitem.headline: Urals trade at distressed level due to May avails.

text.p: Russian Urals were under pressure on Wednesday after a prompt cargo of the sour crude changed hands Tuesday night at a distressed Dated Brent -$1.38, traders said.

The deal involved a May 22-23 cargo sold by a trader to a Spanish refiner. It was preceded by a small May 27-29 loader (65,000-70,000 tonnes) of Urals reported sold at eight cents higher, or Dated Brent -$1.30.

Traders said Urals was assessed in the Dated Brent -$1.40/-$1.30 region on Wednesday, adding later barrels could probably fetch a better price. This compared with Tuesday's early levels of Dated Brent -$1.25/-$1.15 for buyers and sellers respectively.
But one trader said the Dated Brent -$1.40 mark was the real market level for Urals, adding that earlier deals this month done at Dated Brent -$1.18 and -$1.15 proved this point.

Traders have said that buyers were being kept at bay by worsening refining margins from the sudden rise in the price of North Sea benchmark crude Brent, which has gained some $2.50 since the start of this month.
Traders have said that about eight Urals cargoes, mostly third decade May, were on offer on Tuesday.
"There are many other (May) barrels unsold, so that depressed the market," the seller of the first cargo said. "There are no firm buyers out there, there's only some potential buying interest."
He said a trading house that has been trying to find a home for an end-May Urals cargo in the Mediterranean and Europe was also offering it in the United States on Wednesday.
